history.content: Hi, my phone has no service at all—no bars, nothing loads, and I can't send picture messages. Can you help?

I can help you troubleshoot your service issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account
- Your customer ID
- Your full name and date of birth

Once I have this information, I can assist you further.
My name is Sofia Martinez and my phone number is +1-617-555-0148.

Your line is currently suspended, which is why you have no service and cannot send picture messages. However, I see that all your recent bills are paid, and your contract is still active.

I can help you resume your service. Once your line is reactivated, you may need to reboot your device to restore connectivity.

Would you like me to proceed with resuming your line now?
Yes, please go ahead and resume my line.

Your line has been resumed and is now active. Please reboot your phone to restore your service. After restarting, you should have cellular service and be able to send picture messages again.

If you still experience any issues after rebooting, let me know and I can help you further troubleshoot.

history.content: I rebooted my phone as you asked, but I still don't have any service—there are no bars and nothing is loading.

Thank you for letting me know. Since your line is now active but you still have no service, let’s troubleshoot further.

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know if you see any of the following:
- Airplane mode icon (✈️)
- “No SIM” or “SIM error” message
- Any signal bars at all (even if they are empty)
- Any network type indicator (like 5G, 4G, LTE, etc.)

This information will help me determine the next steps to restore your service.
I see the Airplane Mode icon and a 'No Signal' icon in the status bar. It also says data is enabled, but there are still no signal bars.

It looks like Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone, which disables all wireless connections—including cellular service. To restore service, please turn off Airplane Mode.

Once you turn off Airplane Mode, check if your signal bars reappear and if you can use your phone normally. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still have no service after disabling Airplane Mode.
Airplane mode is now off, but I still have no signal—no bars are showing, and nothing is loading.

Thank you for confirming. Since Airplane Mode is off and you still have no signal, the next step is to check your SIM card status. Please check if your phone displays any messages like “No SIM,” “SIM error,” or “SIM locked.” 

If you don’t see any such messages, please try removing and reinserting your SIM card (reseating it), then check if your signal returns.

Let me know if you see any SIM-related messages or if reseating the SIM card restores your service.
I removed and reinserted the SIM card. The phone says the SIM status is active, but there are still no signal bars and nothing is loading.

Thank you for checking the SIM card. Since your SIM status is active but you still have no signal, the next step is to check your phone’s network settings, specifically the APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for network connectivity.

Could you please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if the MMSC URL is missing? If you’re unsure, you can reset your APN settings to default and then reboot your device.

After resetting and rebooting, let me know if your service is restored or if you still have no signal.
I just checked my APN settings and they look normal to me—nothing seems to be missing. Should I still try resetting them and rebooting the phone?

Yes, even if the APN settings look normal, sometimes resetting them to default can resolve hidden configuration issues. Please go ahead and reset your APN settings to default, then reboot your phone.

After rebooting, check if your signal bars appear and if you can use your phone normally. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still have no service after these steps.
I already reset the APN settings to default and rebooted my phone. The device says the changes have been applied, but I still have no signal—no bars are showing and nothing is loading.

Thank you for your patience and for following all the troubleshooting steps so far. Your SIM is active, your device is properly activated, your plan is in good standing, and you have already reset your APN settings and rebooted your phone.

Since you still have no signal after all these steps, this may indicate a deeper technical issue that cannot be resolved through standard troubleshooting.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can investigate this further and provide advanced support.

YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.
